name: Camp Last Ember
region_detail: A shallow coulee in the northern uplands.
site_type: camp | Abandoned infrastructure; supernatural sites | Abandoned wartime encampment.
history: During the closing years of the War of Broken Banners, a detached company of northern soldiers crossed into the eastern uplands. They established a sheltered camp beside a dependable seep, but disappeared before rejoining their regiment. Those who later found the camp reported that its fires were still burning and its horses remained tethered.
current_state: Most canvas has rotted away, and grass conceals the remains of the tents. Several fire pits contain unusually clean ash despite years of exposure. An overturned supply wagon and a locked iron-bound pay chest remain in a sheltered recess. No bodies have been discovered.
inhabitants: Scavenging wildlife; occasional itinerant hunters. The fate of the soldiers and any supernatural occupants remain undetermined.
danger_level: Low on the approach; potentially moderate or high if the circumstances of the disappearance recur.
points_of_interest:
Tent rings; fire pits; tethering stakes; overturned wagon; locked pay chest; fragments of regimental insignia; a seep beneath an overhanging bank.

Unresolved elements: The identity and allegiance of the missing company.; Whether the disappearance was caused by desertion, violence, magic, or another circumstance.; The contents of the pay chest and surviving papers.; Whether the lingering peculiarities of the camp represent an active hazard.
discovery: A shallow coulee in the northern uplands. Veterans drinking at the Last Water exchange conflicting directions to the camp. Surviving regimental records or the old supply route may narrow the search.
